references.text: Moses had previously given instructions that the Lord would show who belonged to him, and now he calls Korah and his assembly to appear before the Lord the next day.
The following verse describes the execution of Moses' command to appear before the Lord with fire pans.
The expression 'tomorrow' is also used when the Lord is to reveal his will through a test or a sign.
The concept of standing 'before the Lord's face' as a judgment or trial occurs several times in the Book of Numbers.
Standing before the Lord is linked to leadership and service in the congregation, which is central to the conflict between Moses, Aaron, and Korah's group.
Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord's face, a parallel to the situation with Korah's rebellion.
